rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to reveal the full elution window, detect any missing late compounds, and gauge whether retention is compressed or truncated. This gives a balanced first map of selectivity and gradient coverage for the 10-compound mixture.

All 10 compounds are already fully resolved, so the only score loss is late elution; the estimated elution window is about phi_e 0.09 to 0.41, so a narrower, lower-organic gradient should pull the last peak earlier while keeping all peaks inside the gradient. I am trimming the window and shortening tG to target t_last under 10 min without sacrificing the currently comfortable minimum resolution.

We are very close to the optimum: all pairs still clear, and only 0.58 min too long. A slightly steeper gradient with a modestly higher phi1 should move the last peak before 10 min while likely keeping the current worst pair resolved above 1.5.

The steepening in injection 3 made pair 6/7 the limiting separation, so this pair is slope-sensitive; I will keep the short run but narrow the window slightly back to phi1 0.70 and raise temperature to recover speed while testing whether a small selectivity shift can lift that pair above 1.5. This targets a full-resolution run with t_last still under 10 min.

Temperature clearly perturbs the critical 6/7 pair strongly, and 45 C was harmful, so I will test the opposite direction at the same fast gradient to seek a favorable selectivity shift while preserving sub-10 min elution. This directly probes whether cooler conditions can restore full resolution without giving back too much runtime.

The best run so far is 12 min at 40 C; since temperature changes strongly alter the crowded middle region, I will pair the gentler 12 min slope with 45 C to test whether the selectivity shift can keep all pairs above 1.5 while bringing the last peak just under 10 min. This is a targeted attempt to improve on injection 2 without over-compressing the critical cluster.

Both hotter and cooler moves from 40 C degraded the critical cluster at 10 min, but temperature clearly changes which pair is limiting; a smaller downward step from the current best conditions is the next most informative selectivity probe. Keeping the successful 12 min slope and window while shifting to 30 C tests whether we can gain a favorable reordering/separation and still stay near the 10 min target.

The selectivity optimum is clearly near 40 C but asymmetric, with cooler temperatures much worse; the remaining path to beat injection 2 is likely a slightly hotter run that trims retention without the severe collapse seen at 45 C with the steeper 10 min gradient. This tests whether 50 C on the gentler 12 min program can push t_last below 10 min while preserving enough spacing in the critical mid-cluster.

At 40 C the separation is safest, and the key issue is only shaving ~0.6 min from the last peak; lowering phi1 slightly should steepen the late part less aggressively for the crowded middle while keeping the effective window closer to the actual elution range. This tests whether a modestly narrower window can preserve the strong 40 C selectivity and still move the last peak toward 10 min.

Injection 2 is still best, and changing phi1 downward made the run slower while 10 min at higher phi1 over-compressed the critical 6/7 pair. The logical interpolation is to keep 40 C and try a slightly higher phi1 at the gentler 12 min slope, aiming to bring t_last under 10 min while retaining enough resolution margin for the mid-cluster.

We already have the maximum CRF, so the only useful exploration is to map the nearby plateau and robustness around the optimum. This small increase in phi1 tests whether a slightly stronger late gradient preserves full resolution while keeping the last peak under 10 min.

The optimum at 12 min has only a small margin on the critical 6/7 pair, and pushing phi1 higher reduced that margin. A slightly longer gradient at the same window and temperature should improve robustness around the critical pair while likely remaining at or very near the score plateau.

Since the optimum is already found, the best remaining use of injections is to probe robustness in the local neighborhood. Raising phi0 slightly tests whether the early part of the gradient can be trimmed without hurting the critical mid-cluster, potentially revealing another full-score setting.

A second full-score method was found by raising phi0, so I will continue moving phi0 upward at the same successful phi1, tG, and temperature to define the robust high-scoring region. This tests whether further trimming the early low-organic segment can maintain full resolution and sub-10 min elution.

The data show a narrow optimum ridge: increasing phi0 helped up to 0.15, while increasing either phi0 too far or phi1 alone reduced the 6/7 margin. Combining the successful phi0 0.15 with slightly higher phi1 0.80 tests whether we can retain full resolution and perhaps gain a shorter, equally optimal robust alternative.

Two full-score points exist at phi1 0.75 with phi0 0.10 and 0.15, while moving phi1 upward hurts the critical 6/7 pair; the missing local check is whether phi0 0.15 with slightly lower phi1 preserves the optimum. This maps the lower side of the plateau and tests whether the full-score region extends toward a narrower gradient window.

The full-score plateau is established near phi1 0.75 at 40 C, and phi0 has only been explored upward from 0.10. Testing phi0 0.05 at the same phi1 and tG maps the lower side of that plateau and checks whether the optimum extends to a more retentive start composition.

The 12 min, 40 C plateau is centered near phi1 0.75, with 0.80 slightly over-compressing the critical pair; testing 0.85 completes the local boundary on the strong-solvent side. This will define how sharply the optimum falls off as the late gradient becomes more aggressive.

The optimum plateau at 12 min is now well mapped; the remaining informative axis is whether the higher-phi0 optimum at 0.15 can tolerate a shorter gradient better than the 0.10 start did. This directly tests if the same full-score selectivity can be retained at 10 min with the later starting composition.

We have multiple full-score methods at 40 C, but temperature shifts strongly affect the critical cluster and robustness around the phi0 0.15 optimum has not been checked. A modest increase to 45 C tests whether this alternate optimum is temperature-tolerant or collapses like the phi0 0.10 methods.

The higher-temperature test badly collapsed the critical 6/7 pair, so the complementary robustness check is the lower side at 35 C for the other full-score method. This will complete the temperature map around the phi0 0.15 optimum and confirm whether 40 C is a sharp selectivity maximum.

We have mapped phi0 and phi1 separately around the 12 min, 40 C optimum, but not their combined lower-phi0/higher-phi1 corner. This run checks whether the broader window can still sit on the full-score plateau or whether the critical 6/7 pair deteriorates as suggested by the one-factor moves.

The remaining unexplored corner near the 40 C optimum is the combined high-phi0/low-phi1 setting, which should define the other edge of the local plateau. This checks whether trimming both ends together preserves enough separation of the critical 6/7 pair while shortening the late region.

Injection 23 found another full-score point with even slightly better critical-pair margin than the earlier optima, so the next step is to test whether the plateau extends to an even narrower window on the low-phi1 side. This probes the boundary of the robust optimum region while keeping the successful temperature and slope fixed.

Injection 23 suggests a particularly robust optimum at phi0 0.20, phi1 0.70, and the final useful experiment is to test the next higher phi0 at the same successful window to locate the upper plateau boundary.
